title: Quasi-coherent modules under an affine morphism
statement: Let $u:U\to X$ be an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and write $\mathcal A=u_*\mathcal O_U$, a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras through $u^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to u_*\mathcal O_U$. An *$\mathcal A$-module* is a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules on $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], regarded as an $\mathcal O_X$-module through $u^\sharp$; morphisms of $\mathcal A$-modules are the $\mathcal A$-linear maps. An $\mathcal A$-module $\mathcal G$ is *quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module* if every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $W$ with an exact sequence $\bigoplus_{j\in J}\mathcal A|_W\to\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal A|_W\to\mathcal G|_W\to0$ of $\mathcal A|_W$-modules for some sets $I,J$; quasi-coherence of $\mathcal O_X$- and $\mathcal O_U$-modules is that of [pqf-def-coherent]. For an $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$ the pushforward $u_*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is an $\mathcal A$-module, $\mathcal A(V)=\mathcal O_U(u^{-1}V)$ acting on $(u_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(u^{-1}V)$. Then: (1) an $\mathcal A$-module is quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal A$-module if and only if its underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent; (2) for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$, $u_*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-module, and $\mathcal F\mapsto u_*\mathcal F$ is an equivalence from the category of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules ($\mathcal O_U$-linear maps) to the category of quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$-modules ($\mathcal A$-linear maps); (3) a quasi-inverse is $\mathcal G\mapsto h(\mathcal G)=u^*\mathcal G\otimes_{u^*\mathcal A}\mathcal O_U$, where $u^*$ is the pullback of [def-pc-module-pullback], $u^*\mathcal A=\mathcal O_U\otimes_{u^{-1}\mathcal O_X}u^{-1}\mathcal A$ is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_U$-algebras, $u^*\mathcal G$ is a $u^*\mathcal A$-module through $(b\otimes a)(b'\otimes g)=bb'\otimes ag$, $\mathcal O_U$ is a $u^*\mathcal A$-algebra through the counit $\epsilon:u^*\mathcal A=u^*u_*\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_U$, and $\otimes_{u^*\mathcal A}$ is the change of rings of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; precisely, the natural maps $\alpha_{\mathcal F}:h(u_*\mathcal F)\to\mathcal F$ induced by the counit $u^*u_*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ and $\beta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to u_*h(\mathcal G)$ adjoint to $u^*\mathcal G\to h(\mathcal G)$, $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, are isomorphisms of $\mathcal O_U$-modules and of $\mathcal A$-modules respectively.

proof.text: Quasi-coherence of the direct-image algebra follows from affine relative Spec. Apply scalar restriction to obtain clause (1).
An affine morphism is quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated. Apply qcqs pushforward quasi-coherence and clause (1) to get clause (2), without using any base-change assertion.

Choose the tensor pushout, extension-of-scalars functors, and canonical maps using affine_module_tensor_construction. Apply affine_module_tensor_comparison_isIso to these exact data to obtain invertibility on quasi-coherent objects.

Lift R and H to the full quasi-coherent subcategories using the preservation assertions. Lift the components of α and β to natural isomorphisms with ObjectProperty.isoMk and NatIso.ofComponents; naturality follows from the original transformations. Use CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk with the inverse of α and inverse of β. Both inclusion comparisons are reflexive isomorphisms. Reassemble all witnesses and conjuncts of the original statement.
